publications.title: Hybrid feature selection with SHAP-based explainable AI for interpretable phishing website detection
publications.venue: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
publications.summary: The paper proposes a phishing website detection framework combining hybrid feature selection and explainable AI. The publisher abstract identifies interpretability, redundant feature representations, and evaluation practices that can produce overly optimistic estimates as concerns.
publications.verification: publisher-version-of-record-and-abstract-verified; detailed metric values should be imported from article tables
publications.research_problem: Phishing website classifiers can perform well while remaining difficult to interpret; redundant feature sets and evaluation leakage can also produce overly optimistic estimates.

methodology.evaluation: 10-fold stratified cross-validation; feature selection carried out independently inside each fold.

publications.findings: The authors report a substantial reduction in feature dimensionality while maintaining predictive performance comparable to use of all features. The publisher abstract does not provide a single universal accuracy value; do not invent one.
limitations_and_review_fields: Record dataset provenance, collection period, class balance, feature extraction, external-validation protocol, and any limitations reported by the authors.
publications.relevance: High relevance to explainable phishing detection, leakage-aware feature selection, and cross-dataset evaluation.
publications.license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 stated on the publisher page; verify third-party figure rights before reuse.

publications.title: EXPLICATE: Enhancing Phishing Detection through Explainable AI and LLM-Powered Interpretability
publications.summary: The authors describe an ML phishing classifier, a dual LIME/SHAP explanation layer, and an LLM layer using DeepSeek V3 to translate technical explanations into natural language. The abstract reports author-reported accuracy and explanation-quality metrics.
publications.verification: arXiv repository record verified; metrics are author-reported preprint claims
publications.research_problem: Make phishing-classification decisions understandable to security analysts and end users rather than presenting a black-box label.
publications.methodology: Three components: domain-feature ML classifier; dual explanation using LIME and SHAP; and a DeepSeek V3 language-model layer that turns technical feature explanations into natural language.

findings.note: All figures are claims reported in the preprint abstract; retain the preprint label and evaluate the experimental protocol before treating them as benchmarks.

limitations_and_review_fields: Check external validation and dataset diversity.
Review how explanation quality and consistency were measured, and whether user studies were performed.

publications.title: Energy-Aware Edge Computing Optimization for Real-Time Anomaly Detection in IoT Networks
publications.summary: The publisher abstract describes energy modelling, adaptive resource allocation, lightweight ML, and offloading across 16 heterogeneous edge devices. It reports author-stated energy and detection-performance results; data are available from the authors upon reasonable request.
publications.verification: publisher record and abstract verified; quantitative values are author-reported
publications.research_problem: Maintain real-time anomaly detection in resource-constrained IoT edge environments while reducing energy consumption.
publications.methodology: The abstract describes a calibrated energy model for heterogeneous edge devices, adaptive resource allocation, lightweight machine learning, and computation offloading. The reported testbed contains 16 heterogeneous edge devices.

findings.author_reported_battery_life_extension: up to 165% in selected energy-constrained scenarios
findings.note: Values are reported by the authors in the publisher abstract; preserve the testbed and comparison context.

publications.data_availability: The publisher states that analysed datasets are available from the authors upon reasonable request.
limitations_and_review_fields: Inspect device heterogeneity and traffic composition.
Check baseline configuration, repeatability, latency and energy measurement procedures.
Assess external generalisability beyond the 16-device testbed.

publications.title: Mitigating Cyber Threats: Machine Learning and Explainable AI for Phishing Detection
publications.summary: The publisher abstract lists XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, KNN, Twin SVM, and CNN evaluated on four public datasets, with LIME for interpretability. The abstract reports XGBoost accuracy of 99.65%.
publications.verification: publisher article record and abstract verified; metric is author-reported
publications.research_problem: Combine phishing detection with explanations of how the model reaches its classification decision.
publications.methodology: The publisher abstract identifies XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, k-nearest neighbours, Twin Support Vector Machine, and convolutional neural networks evaluated on four public datasets; LIME is used for explanation.

findings.note: Author-reported abstract value; retain the four-dataset and protocol context and confirm exact per-dataset results in the paper.

limitations_and_review_fields: Check identities and provenance of the four datasets.
Review leakage controls, split strategy, class balance, external validation and explanation stability.

publications.title: EKT-XAI: Efficient Kolmogorov-Arnold Network Transformer for Lightweight Smishing Detection with Explainable AI
publications.summary: The publisher abstract describes KAN layers in a transformer for SMS phishing detection, with attention visualisation, LIME, KAN activation analysis, and decision-path tracing. The abstract identifies SMS Spam Collection and SMS Phishing datasets and reports author-stated results.
publications.verification: publisher record and abstract verified; metrics are author-reported
publications.research_problem: Detect SMS phishing while making model decisions interpretable and keeping inference efficient for mobile deployment.
publications.methodology: KAN layers are integrated into a transformer architecture. The abstract describes attention visualisation, LIME attribution, KAN activation-pattern analysis and decision-path tracing. Evaluation uses the SMS Spam Collection (5,574 messages) and SMS Phishing Dataset (5,971 messages).

findings.note: The abstract also reports ablation improvements for KAN layers and attention. Keep all metrics linked to the dataset and protocol, not as a generic model badge.

limitations_and_review_fields: Inspect dataset construction, duplicates, contamination and split design.
Check latency, model size, device-level energy use and mobile hardware validation.
Review comparisons with baseline systems and robustness to newly emerging smishing messages.
